Banded_Chlorosis.quote: Banded chlorosis is a physiological disorder caused by cold injury, characterized by horizontal areas of light green to white tissue that extends in a narrow (2-4 inch) band across the leaf.

Brown_Spot.quote: In leaves, elongate, reddish-brown lesions with an obvious yellow "halo" develop parallel to veins.

Eye_Spot.quote: The first observable symptoms are minute water-soaked spots that usually occur on young leaves.

Grassy_Shoot.quote: Young leaves become pale in colour and appear thin and narrow.
The plants appear bushy and 'grass-like' due to reduction in the length of internodes, premature and continuous tillering, and the affected clumps are stunted.

Leaf_Mosaic_Virus.quote: Mosaic symptoms such as irregular chlorosis and mottling were observed in the leaves of infected plants.

Leaf_Scald.quote: During the chronic form, pencil lines, bleaching and necrosis will progressively appear on leaves before scalding of stalks and stalk death.

Pokkah_Boeng.quote: Symptoms on sugar cane include chlorosis and necrosis of leaves, punctured lesions, twisted leaves, reduction of the total leaf area, death of the top of the plant and stalk rot.

Red_Spot.quote: minute red spots appear on the centre of the mid-rib and develop in both directions forming small or long lesions.
Initial symptoms are red spots on midribs, which gradually expand, forming elongated red lesions.

Sett_Rot.quote: The disease primarily affects the setts usually two to three weeks after planting; the internal tissues turn red, and then brownish-black with a characteristic pineapple smell.

Yellow_Leaf.quote: Sugarcane yellow leaf virus (SCYLV) causes sugarcane yellow leaf disease (SCYLD), characterized by intense yellowing of leaf midribs and tissue necrosis.
